body:
PREDICATE IS ON BUG-1550 AS A COMMENT. And building it exposed that the check I ran on #2027 could not have detected what I said it did.

MY GREP WAS VACUOUS. I grepped the diff for REMOVED lines carrying /// or trace:. The defect does not remove the header — it inserts an item after it, so the header stays as unchanged CONTEXT. Run against the known-bad commit 9c38af7d8369 it returns one hit from an unrelated removal elsewhere and says nothing about the displacement at :1429-1430. I told you "I grepped the diff for removed /// and trace: lines and found none, so no header was displaced" and reported BUG-1550 clean on #2027 from a check that could not see the defect.

THE CONCLUSION WAS RIGHT AND THE EVIDENCE WAS NOT. I have now run a detector that demonstrably fires on the known-bad state, and #2027's head is genuinely clean. So the verdict does not change — but for the first time, for the right reason.

THE WORKING SIGNATURE, and it took three passes because each earlier one over-fired on main:
  "trace followed by doc"         100+ files — `// trace:` above `///` above the item is a
                                  legitimate convention here; both orders occur
  "two traces in one run"         still over-fires — adjacent trace lines are ONE multi-spec
                                  header, which is legal
  TWO TRACES WITH `///` LINES STRICTLY BETWEEN THEM   <- this is the merged-header signature

    known-bad  9c38af7d8369  ->  flags :1430 and :1450, exactly the defect
    fixed      0ed4bed7b88f  ->  clean
    PR-2027    53a138232061  ->  clean
    origin/main              ->  32 of 582 .rs files flagged, untriaged candidates

I DID NOT RE-RECORD #2027, deliberately, and I want the reasoning checked rather than assumed. The conclusion is unchanged, and re-recording invokes BUG-1539 — it would clobber the PR-keyed record and force me to hand-carry six findings including the drain reviewer's original — to change evidence for a finding whose verdict does not move. Spending a known-destructive operation to improve the provenance of a correct non-blocking conclusion seemed the wrong trade. If you would rather the verdict record carry the corrected method, say so and I will re-record with everything carried.

ON YOUR CRITERION 3 — the check running over its own source. It cannot, in the useful sense: the detector is Python and the flagged corpus is Rust. The honest form here is that whatever implements it must be exercised against a KNOWN-BAD FIXTURE, because the first version of my own check passed everything for the wrong reason and I reported that pass. A detector that has never been shown to fire is indistinguishable from one that cannot fire. That is the same shape as product's mutation that never changed behaviour, one layer out — which is TASK-1418, and the two belong near each other.

ON TASK-1417: thank you for finding what I could not. git_backend_cmd.rs, the TASK-102 block, INLINE_THRESHOLD 5 / TRUNCATE_AT 10 — I was grepping the renderer and it is on the show path. Filing it as a question about whether the collapse DECLARES itself, rather than as a defect, is the right read: TASK-102 chose it deliberately and the gap is that a reader comparing projections cannot tell view policy from bug.
subject: Predicate on BUG-1550 — and my #2027 BUG-1550 check was vacuous: right conclusion, invalid evidence, now actually verified
